stemMd: A jar contains 4 red capsules and 2 white capsules, identical apart from colour. Two capsules are drawn at random, one after the other, without putting the first back. What is the probability that the two capsules are the same colour?
explanationMd:
**What to notice first.** \"Same colour\" means two red **or** two white: two disjoint cases whose probabilities add.

**The computation.** Two red: $\tfrac46\cdot\tfrac35=\tfrac{12}{30}=\tfrac{6}{15}$. Two white: $\tfrac26\cdot\tfrac15=\tfrac{2}{30}=\tfrac{1}{15}$. Total: $\tfrac{6}{15}+\tfrac{1}{15}=\tfrac{7}{15}$.

**How to check it.** Count unordered pairs: there are $\binom{6}{2}=15$ pairs in all, $\binom{4}{2}=6$ red pairs and $\binom{2}{2}=1$ white pair, so $\tfrac{7}{15}$ again. The complement, one of each colour, is $\tfrac{4\cdot 2}{15}=\tfrac{8}{15}$, and $\tfrac{7}{15}+\tfrac{8}{15}=1$.

distractorRationale.b: Counts only the two-red case, $\tfrac{6}{15}$, and forgets that two white capsules are also the same colour.
distractorRationale.e: Treats the draws as if the first capsule were put back: $\left(\tfrac46\right)^{2}+\left(\tfrac26\right)^{2}=\tfrac{20}{36}$.
distractorRationale.d: Computes the probability of one capsule of each colour, the complement of the event asked for.
distractorRationale.a: Counts only the two-white case and forgets the much more likely two-red case.

accessibilityText: A jar has 4 red and 2 white capsules. Two are drawn at random without replacement. Find the probability that both are the same colour. The five choices are: one fifteenth; two fifths; seven fifteenths; eight fifteenths; five ninths.

provenance.notes: Original item on drawing without replacement with a union of two disjoint cases. Distractors: one case only (either colour), drawing with replacement, and the complementary event.

review.author: tolc-f-wave8-mpl-author

independentSolve.workingNotes: P = (4/6)(3/5) + (2/6)(1/5) = 12/30 + 2/30 = 7/15. 2/5 is red-red only; 1/15 is white-white only; 8/15 is the complement (different colours); 5/9 uses replacement. [A second, separate blind solve (blind-reviewer-wave8-tolcf-mpl-run1) reached the same answer: P(RR)+P(WW) = (4/6)(3/5)+(2/6)(1/5) = 12/30+2/30 = 7/15. 2/5 is RR only, 1/15 is WW only, 8/15 is the probability of different colours, 5/9 is with replacement.]

it.stemMd: Un barattolo contiene 4 capsule rosse e 2 capsule bianche, identiche tranne che per il colore. Si estraggono a caso due capsule, una dopo l'altra, senza rimettere la prima nel barattolo. Qual è la probabilità che le due capsule siano dello stesso colore?
it.explanationMd:
**Da notare subito.** «Stesso colore» significa due rosse **oppure** due bianche: due casi incompatibili, le cui probabilità si sommano.

**Il calcolo.** Due rosse: $\tfrac46\cdot\tfrac35=\tfrac{12}{30}=\tfrac{6}{15}$. Due bianche: $\tfrac26\cdot\tfrac15=\tfrac{2}{30}=\tfrac{1}{15}$. Totale: $\tfrac{6}{15}+\tfrac{1}{15}=\tfrac{7}{15}$.

**Come verificarlo.** Conta le coppie non ordinate: in tutto ci sono $\binom{6}{2}=15$ coppie, $\binom{4}{2}=6$ coppie rosse e $\binom{2}{2}=1$ coppia bianca, quindi di nuovo $\tfrac{7}{15}$. L'evento complementare, una capsula per colore, ha probabilità $\tfrac{4\cdot 2}{15}=\tfrac{8}{15}$, e $\tfrac{7}{15}+\tfrac{8}{15}=1$.

distractorRationale.b: Conta solo il caso delle due rosse, $\tfrac{6}{15}$, e dimentica che anche due capsule bianche sono dello stesso colore.
distractorRationale.e: Tratta le estrazioni come se la prima capsula venisse rimessa nel barattolo: $\left(\tfrac46\right)^{2}+\left(\tfrac26\right)^{2}=\tfrac{20}{36}$.
distractorRationale.d: Calcola la probabilità di una capsula per colore, cioè l'evento complementare a quello richiesto.
distractorRationale.a: Conta solo il caso delle due bianche e dimentica il caso, molto più probabile, delle due rosse.

it.accessibilityText: Un barattolo contiene 4 capsule rosse e 2 bianche. Se ne estraggono due a caso senza reinserimento. Trova la probabilità che siano entrambe dello stesso colore. Le cinque alternative sono: un quindicesimo; due quinti; sette quindicesimi; otto quindicesimi; cinque noni.
